thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate detected on Dedicated routing layer for customer AtlasFin across us-west-2. Error spike started ~few mins ago, autoscale not resolving.

Alex (oncall-sre): I’m on it. tailing router logs now. Seen a surge of `RUNTIME_ERROR: upstream connection reset` from pool dedicated-usw2-3.

Sam (Account Manager): Heads-up — AtlasFin is Tier-1 enterprise with active scheduled deploy this week; primary contacts are in the account doc. I’ll start outreach if we hit 15m.

Olivia (Customer Success): Please flag if we need a customer-facing note. I can draft and route through Sam.

Alex (oncall-sre): Quick mitigation attempt: scaling down the problematic pool and routing traffic to fallback pool dedicated-usw2-1. Running command now: `redwoodctl pool rotate --from dedicated-usw2-3 --to dedicated-usw2-1 --drain 60s`

incident-bot: Command accepted. Rotation job 6723 started.

Alex (oncall-sre): Rotation in progress, drain at 60s. Error rate dropping for a subset of requests. Still seeing 502 on requests hitting shard 7. Collecting pprof and router logs, pushing to /tmp/atlasfin-routing-pprof.tar.gz

Oliver (IC): Noted. Create an internal status line we can paste to status page and customer email — short and factual.

Katie (PM): For internal exec comms we’ll need: impact summary, systems affected, estimated ETA, mitigation steps, and which accounts are impacted. Add contact routing (who to page) too.

Sam (Account Manager): AtlasFin contacts: primary-AM Sam (sam@redwood.ai), primary-ops ops-lead@atlasfin.com, escalation CTO cto@atlasfin.com. Routing: primary via email + phone, escalation SMS.

Olivia (Customer Success): Also impacted: two subaccounts under AtlasFin (atlasfin-payments, atlasfin-data). Billing unaffected, but API request/response failures for model inference.

Alex (oncall-sre): Root cause hypothesis: connection pooling regression in recent runtime patch that changes keepalive behavior for dedicated pools. Repro on staging when simulating long-lived streams. Rolling back to previous kernel in the affected pool now.

incident-bot: Status changed to INVESTIGATING. Severity: sev2 (customer-facing degraded).

Katie (PM): Draft status page update (short):
```
We are investigating increased error rates for inference requests for AtlasFin on dedicated-us-west-2. We are actively routing traffic away from the impacted capacity and working on a configuration rollback. Some requests may fail with 5xx. We will provide updates within 15 minutes.
```

Sam (Account Manager): Draft customer email (concise, empathetic):
```
Hi AtlasFin team — we’re investigating a service disruption impacting inference requests for your dedicated cluster in us-west-2. Our engineers are routing traffic to alternate capacity and applying a configuration rollback. You may see transient 5xx errors. We’ll share an update within 15 minutes and will coordinate directly if you need assistance. — Sam, Redwood
```

Olivia (Customer Success): Internal support template for CS inbox:
```
Short summary: AtlasFin dedicated cluster experiencing elevated 5xx. Workaround: automatic routing to fallback pool in progress. ETA: unknown, engineers rolling back recent runtime patch. If customers ask: escalate to Sam (AM) and CC oncall (Alex).
```

Mike (Security): Any chance this is a malicious connection storm? Check auth failures and unusual token use. I’ll review logs and let you know.

Alex (oncall-sre): No auth anomalies so far — tokens validated fine. Pattern looks like connection timeouts + half-closed sockets from our runtime after long-lived prompts.

Oliver (IC): Action items: 1) Alex - finish rollback for pool dedicated-usw2-3 (in progress). 2) Alex - confirm routing completed and error rate baseline. 3) Sam - prep customer email and send after we confirm routing. 4) Olivia - update CS canned responses. 5) Mike - sign off on security review. 6) Katie - prepare exec note if duration >30m.

Alex (oncall-sre): Rollback finished on pool dedicated-usw2-3 at ~now. Error rate showing 80% reduction for affected shard. Continuing monitoring for 10m.

incident-bot: Rotation job 6723 completed.

Sam (Account Manager): Sending curated note to AtlasFin ops (will BCC exec). Copy of email: `Sent to ops-lead@atlasfin.com, cto@atlasfin.com`

Olivia (Customer Success): CS inbox updated with canned response and link to this thread.

Mike (Security): Security review: no suspicious auth or token reuse; no indicators of compromise.

Katie (PM): Status page update (follow-up):
```
Update: Traffic rerouted and configuration rollback applied. Error rates have substantially decreased for AtlasFin; we continue to monitor. If you still see failures, please contact your account team directly.
```

Oliver (IC): Internal exec note (one-liner for SLT):
`AtlasFin experienced a routing-related inference disruption in us-west-2; mitigation (rollback + routing) reduced errors; monitoring. No data exposure suspected. Timeline 00:00–~00:12 (ongoing validation).`

Alex (oncall-sre): Monitoring window complete, error rate stable at baseline. Closing incident but keeping postmortem open to verify regression and add a rollback gating test.

incident-bot: Status changed to RESOLVED. Please file postmortem and set follow-up: add e2e test for keepalive behavior in dedicated pools.

Sam (Account Manager): I pinged AtlasFin with final summary and remediation plan. They appreciated the quick response.

Olivia (Customer Success): Closing loop with CS and updating the customer escalations doc with contact routing confirmation.

Oliver (IC): Postmortem owners: Alex (root cause & remediation), Katie (customer comms timeline), Sam (customer impact verification). Please assign within 24h.

Alex (oncall-sre): Assigned. I’ll attach logs, pprof and the rollback diff to the postmortem.

Sam (Account Manager): Thanks all. Good triage. :thumbsup:
